figures.cap: triangle with sides 36 m, 30 m, 10 m and angle theta

parts.latex:
For the triangle below, what is the value of $\theta$, to the nearest degree?

\exfigure{719_q8_1}

solutions.latex:
The three sides are known, and $\theta$ is opposite the side of length $30$ m. Use the cosine rule.
$$\begin{aligned} \cos\theta &= \dfrac{36^2+10^2-30^2}{2\times 36\times 10} \\ &= \dfrac{496}{720} \\ &\approx 0.6889 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \theta &\approx 46.4^\circ \\ &\approx 46^\circ \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is option A.

719_q8_1.notes: Triangle with sides 36 m, 30 m and 10 m. Theta is marked with an arc at the bottom-left vertex, ending on both arms. Labels are kept at the crop's small print size and clear of the lines. Drawn to the crop's proportions, not to scale (rule 1). Rules 1,2,3,11,14.

parts.latex:
Find the size of the largest angle in this triangle, giving answer correct to the nearest degree.

\exfigure{2839_q1b_1}

solutions.latex:
The largest angle is opposite the longest side (20), so use the cosine rule for that angle $A$.
$$\begin{aligned}\cos A &= \dfrac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{2bc} \\ &= \dfrac{16^2+13^2-20^2}{2\times 16\times 13} \\ &= \dfrac{25}{416} \\ \therefore \angle A &= 86.55\ldots^\circ \\ &= 87^\circ \text{ (to the nearest degree)}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Uses the cosine rule correctly, or equivalent merit

Which calculation finds the value of the smallest angle in the triangle below?

\exfigure{2837_q4a_1}

solutions.latex:
The smallest angle is opposite the shortest side, which is the $10$ mm side.

By the cosine rule, with $\theta$ opposite the side $10$, the other two sides are $16$ and $18$:
$$\cos\theta = \dfrac{16^2 + 18^2 - 10^2}{2 \times 16 \times 18}$$
This matches option C. Options A, B and D place a different side opposite $\theta$, so they find a different angle.

parts.latex: A triangle has sides 12m, 14m and 16m. What is the largest angle of the triangle?

solutions.latex:
The largest angle is opposite the longest side (16 m). Using the cosine rule:
$$\begin{aligned} \cos\theta &= \dfrac{14^2 + 12^2 - 16^2}{2 \times 12 \times 14} \\ &= 0.25 \end{aligned}$$
$$\theta = \cos^{-1}(0.25) = 75^\circ 31'$$
This matches option C.

solutions.latex:
Using the cosine rule, with $\theta$ opposite the side of length $33.2$ cm:

$$\cos C=\dfrac{a^2+b^2-c^2}{2ab}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \cos\theta &= \dfrac{51^2+24^2-33.2^2}{2(51)(24)} \\ &= 0.847\ldots \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \theta &= \cos^{-1}(0.847\ldots) \\ &\approx 32.055\ldots^\circ \end{aligned}$$

figures.cap: triangle XYZ with sides 48 km, 65 km, 89 km

solutions.latex:
In $\triangle XYZ$ the side opposite $\angle YXZ$ is $YZ = 89$ km, so use the cosine rule.
$$\begin{aligned} \cos \angle YXZ &= \dfrac{48^2+65^2-89^2}{2\times 48\times 65} \\ &= -0.22307\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \angle YXZ &= \cos^{-1}(-0.22307\ldots) \\ &\approx 102.89^\circ \\ &\approx 102^\circ 53' \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the answer is option B}$$

7443.stem:
A block of land is in the shape of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ shown below. The diagonal $AC$ has been drawn.

\exfigure{264_q31_1}

The following measurement have been taken:

$AD = 75$ m, $BC = 90$ m.

$D$ is 135 m due south of $B$.

$\angle CAD = 53^\circ$ and $\angle ACD = 32^\circ$.

figures.cap: quadrilateral ABCD with diagonal AC and north line BD

parts.latex: Find the length of $CD$. (Answer correct to the nearest metre.)
Find the size of $\angle CBD$. (Answer correct to the nearest degree.)

solutions.latex:
In $\triangle ACD$, the angle sum gives
$$\begin{aligned} \angle ADC &= 180^\circ-53^\circ-32^\circ \\ &= 95^\circ \end{aligned}$$
CD is opposite $\angle CAD=53^\circ$ and $AD$ is opposite $\angle ACD=32^\circ$, so by the sine rule
$$\dfrac{CD}{\sin 53^\circ}=\dfrac{75}{\sin 32^\circ}$$
$$\begin{aligned} CD &= \dfrac{75\sin 53^\circ}{\sin 32^\circ} \\ &\approx 113.03 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ CD\approx 113 \text{ m}$$
criteria: Sets up the sine rule correctly, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
In $\triangle BCD$ the three sides are known: $BC=90$, $BD=135$, $CD\approx 113$. Use the cosine rule for the angle at $B$, opposite $CD$.
$$\begin{aligned} \cos\angle CBD &= \dfrac{BC^2+BD^2-CD^2}{2\times BC\times BD} \\ &= \dfrac{90^2+135^2-113^2}{2\times 90\times 135} \\ &\approx 0.5580 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \angle CBD &\approx 56.1^\circ \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \angle CBD\approx 56^\circ$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

meta.self_check: Python: 56.09 with CD=113, 56.11 with unrounded CD.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{264_q31_s1}

$D$ is due south of $B$, so $BD$ lies along the north-south line through $B$, pointing south ($180^\circ$). $C$ is east of this line, and $\angle CBD\approx 56^\circ$ from the south direction.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Bearing of } C \text{ from } B &= 180^\circ-56^\circ \\ &= 124^\circ \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{bearing}=124^\circ\text{T}$$

meta.self_check: Bearing measured clockwise from north; C is to the south-east of B.
meta.generated_note: Uses the rounded 56 degrees from part (b).

264_q31_1.notes: Quadrilateral ABCD with diagonal AC. The dashed north line runs through B and D, with a gap for the 135 m label and a filled N arrow at the top. Angle arcs are centred on A (53°) and C (32°) and end on the arms. Vertices and labels sit at the crop's positions. Round 2 used a smaller label font, moved the 53° label off AD and enlarged the 32° arc. The house arrowhead is smaller than the crop's large N arrow (rule 4). Rules 1, 3, 4, 11, 14, 22.

264_q31_s1.notes: New sketch drawn to scale: BD=135 vertical, BC=90 at 56° to south, so CD comes out at 112.9 (labelled ≈113 m). The dashed north line above B has an arrow and N; there is a dashed extension below D. The 56° arc is between BD and BC. The 124° bearing arc runs clockwise from north to BC, with its arrowhead ending on BC. Labels clear of the lines. Rules 4, 11, 14, 22.
